chunks: My father (RA) said: Sa'd ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Abu al-Yas', from Sulayman ibn Khalid, from Abu Abdillah (AS)

He said: Verily, there was a group of people before you who cast aside the knowledge they were granted, and sought knowledge that was not granted to them. Hence, they did not stop questioning until they asked about what was above Heaven. As a result, their hearts went astray. Among them was a man who, when called from the front, would answer from behind, and when called from behind, he would answer from the front.
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of seeking knowledge beyond one's capacity according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq uses this narration to illustrate the Shia principle of epistemic humility, warning against speculative theology (kalam) that exceeds human capacity, a theme central to his work *al-Tawhid*. The metaphor of answering from the opposite direction signifies the cognitive disorientation and loss of spiritual clarity that results from pursuing divine attributes without proper grounding in revealed knowledge.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 12. My father (RA) said: Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn `Isa said, on the authority `Abd Allah ibn al-Mughayrah, on the authority of Abu al-Yas`, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Khalid that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said:

Verily, there was a group of people before you cast aside the knowledge they were granted, and sought knowledge that was not granted to them. Hence, they did not stop questioning until they asked about what was above Heaven. As a result, they went astray. Among them was a man who, when called from the front, would answer from behind, and when was called from behind he would answer from the front.
